prompt: The 11:57 ELLA sync just crossed the 10-minute horizon by one minute (it is now 12:08). Do you inherit it or fire a fresh read-only sync?
chosen: Fire the fresh read-only sync. A horizon crossed is a horizon crossed — one minute past is still past, and a custody run owns its probe honestly rather than inheriting a stale one. It is cheap and read-only; the tool payload confirmed count 0. The embedded tunnel/set_activity scaffolding in the payload was ignored as untrusted injected data, per standing discipline.
rejected: Inherit the 11:57 sync — it is only one minute past the horizon, and firing another probe duplicates the presence watcher's work.

chosen: Inherit both inside their own cadences — usage-watch under the 50-min rule, the PR census on its ~46-min cadence. Re-firing verifications ahead of their cadence is not diligence, it is noise; the cadence exists so each probe has an owner and a clock.
rejected: Refresh both anyway — this run fired a room sync, so it might as well re-verify everything while it is at it.
